from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Basis Vectors", [

            "Each vector is i, j, and k.",
            "Linear transformation moves these basis vectors."
        ])
        
        # Define vectors and grid
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2]).scale(0.7)
        ihat = Vector(RIGHT, color="#FF5733")
        jhat = Vector(UP, color="#33FF57")
        khat = Vector(OUT, color="#3357FF") # Added k for completeness
        
        # Position the coordinate system in the right area
        area_group = VGroup(axes, ihat, jhat, khat)
        self.place_in_area(area_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(Create(axes))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(GrowArrow(ihat), GrowArrow(jhat), GrowArrow(khat))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Transformations: Shear and Rotation", [
            "Linear transformations keep the origin fixed.",
            "Grid lines remain straight and parallel.",
            "Rotations and shears are common examples."

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Determinants and Volume Scaling", [
            "Determinants measure volume scaling factor.", 
            "A unit cube changes volume accordingly.", 
            "The absolute value shows volume change."
        ])
        
        # Animation setup
        unit_cube = Cube(side_length=1, fill_opacity=0.3, color="#FF4500")
        scaled_shape = Cube(side_length=1.2, fill_opacity=0.3, color="#00CED1")
        det_text = MathTex(r"|\det(A)| = \text{Volume Factor}", color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(unit_cube, 'B2')
        self.play(Create(unit_cube), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(scaled_shape, 'D4')
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(unit_cube, scaled_shape), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(det_text, 'F2')
        self.play(Write(det_text), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-world Application: Computer Graphics", [
            "Matrices chain transformations for complex models.",
            "Used extensively in computer graphics engines.",
            "Multiplication applies movement to 3D objects."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent a 3D object with a 3D axes and a simple shape
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2])
        cube = Cube(side_length=1, fill_opacity=0.5, color="#FF69B4")
        obj_group = VGroup(axes, cube)
        self.place_at_grid(obj_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(obj_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF69B4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a matrix transformation hint
        matrix = Matrix([["x'"], ["y'"], ["z'"]]).scale(0.5).set_color("#7FFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(matrix))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#7FFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotate the cube to show movement
        self.play(Rotate(cube, angle=PI/4, axis=OUT), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Basis Vectors
sections.content: Briefly revisit 3D space defined by standard basis vectors i(1,0,0), j(0,1,0), and k(0,0,1). Explain that a linear transformation is simply where these basis vectors land after a transformation.
sections.example: Imagine three unit-length arrows (axes) anchored at the origin; watch how they move to new positions in 3D space.

sections.title: The Transformation Matrix
sections.content: Introduce the 3x3 matrix as a storage container for the new coordinates of i, j, and k. Column 1 is the new i, Column 2 the new j, and Column 3 the new k.
sections.example: Representing a scaling transformation where the x-axis doubles, y-axis stays, and z-axis triples using a diagonal matrix: diag(2, 1, 3).

sections.title: Visualizing Transformations: Shear and Rotation
sections.content: Demonstrate that linear transformations keep the origin fixed and grid lines parallel. Introduce 3D rotation (e.g., around the z-axis) and shearing (slanting a cube into a parallelepiped).
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Robot Arm' joint rotating a 3D block, or a stack of cards being 'sheared' into a tilted shape.

sections.title: Determinants and Volume Scaling
sections.content: Explain the geometric meaning of the determinant of a 3x3 matrix: it represents the factor by which the transformation scales the volume of any shape.
sections.example: If a unit cube with volume 1 transforms into a parallelepiped with volume 2, the absolute value of the determinant of the transformation matrix is 2.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Computer Graphics
sections.content: Synthesize knowledge by showing how matrices are chained to move complex 3D models in games or engineering software.
sections.example: A 3D character (e.g., a rabbit) being rotated and scaled in a game engine; each frame is just the result of a sequence of matrix-vector multiplications.
